Name: EV1 AC Induction Motor
//: Real EV1 has minimal coast torque without commanded regen —
//1: bearing friction + windage only.  Map Zero Throttle values are
//2: the residual drag scaled to motor RPM.  Coastdown calibration
//3: (2026-04-30) showed engine coast contributes < 10 % of total drag
//4: at typical speeds; the bulk lives in TMeasy slip dynamics.  See
//5: docs/ev1_chrono_audit.md §11 for the calibration history and
//ceiling: TWO DIFFERENT LIMITS — do not conflate them.  This file is
//ceiling1: the DRIVE'S PHYSICAL CAPABILITY and carries only the ceiling
//ceiling2: above which the propulsion system makes no torque.  The EV1's
//ceiling3: ~80 mph top speed is a SOFTWARE CALIBRATION and does NOT belong
//ceiling4: here — it is the propulsion controller's (PIM/PCM) job.
//ceiling5: @source:manual propulsion p250: "The PIM will limit vehicle
//ceiling6: speed in the forward direction to 129 km/h (80 mph) and in the
//ceiling7: reverse direction to 48 km/h (30 mph)."  Modelling that cap as
//ceiling8: motor physics would make a software choice unmodifiable, and the
//ceiling9: software limiting is part of the EV1's character.
//ceiling11: DRIVE-SYSTEM CEILING = 16000 RPM.  Deliberately NOT called a
//ceiling12: 'hardware' or 'mechanical' ceiling: the manual states no rotor
//ceiling13: burst speed, no bearing speed and no inverter frequency limit
//ceiling14: anywhere.  What it states is the speed above which the
//ceiling15: PROPULSION SYSTEM STOPS PRODUCING TORQUE, which is exactly and
//ceiling16: only what a torque map can represent.
//ceiling18: INPUT PULSE RATE TOO HIGH"): "The DTC will set any time the PCM
//ceiling19: sees a pulse rate greater than 34,000 Hz on the speed/direction
//ceiling20: input.  This corresponds to a shaft speed of 16,000 RPM."
//ceiling21: Reaction: SERVICE NOW telltale, DTC stored, PROPULSION DISABLED.
//ceiling22: The threshold is a PULSE RATE and the reaction is a PCM software
//ceiling23: action; 16,000 RPM is GM restating that rate as shaft speed.  The
//ceiling24: same page's Diagnostic Aids list over-speed ("going down a hill")
//ceiling25: as one of five COULD-BE-CAUSED-BY bullets, three of which are
//ceiling26: wiring/supply faults — so the page does not attribute it solely
//ceiling27: to over-speed, it allows over-speed as a genuine cause.
//ceiling28: @inferred: that a torque map should terminate where propulsion is
//ceiling29: commanded off.  16000 RPM / 10.946 / 0.2915 m tyre ~= 100 mph at
//ceiling30: the road: above the 80 mph software cap, 1.25x it, not
//ceiling32: NOTE the same p250 also says the PIM decreases torque current
//ceiling33: "to limit drive motor shaft speed" — shaft-speed limiting is a
//ceiling34: PIM function on the real car.  This map is not that limiter; it
//ceiling35: is the envelope the limiter would act inside.  If a PIM-side
//ceiling36: shaft-speed limiter ever lands (see docs/TODO.md), it acts on
//ceiling37: torque command and this ceiling stays as the backstop.
//ceiling39: WHY BOTH MAPS MUST END AT ZERO: Chrono clamps the map LOOKUP at
//ceiling41: ChFunctionInterp holds the endpoint value beyond the table
//ceiling43: whatever torque sits at the last point of EITHER map is delivered
//ceiling44: at EVERY higher speed, forever.  A non-zero last point is not a
//ceiling45: ceiling — it is unbounded power.  That is true of the coast map
//ceiling46: too: a residual -40 N.m held to infinity is ~202 kW of phantom
//ceiling47: regen at 48,000 RPM, from a drive rated ~102 kW.  Above the
//ceiling48: ceiling the manual says propulsion is DISABLED, so the inverter
//ceiling49: produces no torque of either sign — motoring or regen — and BOTH
//ceiling50: maps ramp to 0 at 16000.  Residual mechanical windage above the
//ceiling51: ceiling is left to the tyre/driveline rather than invented here.
//ceiling52: tests/test_motor_speed_ceiling.cpp pins both endpoints at zero,
//ceiling53: pins Maximal Engine Speed RPM to them, and asserts zero delivered
//ceiling54: torque above the ceiling at EVERY throttle position — not just at
//ceiling55: full throttle, where the coast map multiplies out.
